terminal_rule: A released pay-as-you-go PostgreSQL RDS instance is removed from the instance inventory and incurs no further instance fees.
required_runtime_evidence: DeleteDBInstance returned one accepted provider request identity for the exact clone
a subsequent complete DescribeDBInstances inventory contains zero rows for that exact clone identity
the source RDS identity remains present and unchanged
no replacement clone or other paid resource was created

release_evidence_projection.derivation: The terminal non-accrual conclusion is derived from this frozen provider contract plus the exact DeleteDBInstance accepted-request commitment, the complete exact-ID DescribeDBInstances absence commitment, an unchanged source-instance readback commitment, and new_paid_resource_count=0.
release_evidence_projection.query_instance_bill_role: QueryInstanceBill supplies a delayed historical billing snapshot only. It is not a provider terminal or non-accruing marker.

billing_lag_boundary: Final-cycle charges may appear after release because pay-as-you-go bills can be generated hourly or daily and instance-bill data can lag by about one day; delayed historical charges do not mean the released instance is still accruing.

sources.claim: DeleteDBInstance releases a pay-as-you-go PostgreSQL RDS instance; after release it is removed from the RDS console and no further fees are charged.
Pay-as-you-go billing stops when the resource is released, while final-cycle bills can be generated later.
Instance-bill data can lag by about one day.
